newsitem.title: ITALY: European car sales seen up 6.5 pct in 1996 -Anfia.
newsitem.headline: European car sales seen up 6.5 pct in 1996 -Anfia.

text.p: Overall European car sales in 1996 rose to 12.71 million units, an increase of 6.5 percent over 1995, provisional data from Italian carmakers' association Anfia showed.
Demand in December, with 783,200 units, showed an 8.6 year-on-year increase, Anfia said in a statement.
Excluding Italy, where new registrations rose 0.34 percent to 1.74 million in 1996, the European market ended the year with a rise of 7.5 percent, not far from 1992 record levels, it said.

Among major markets, German sales rose 5.1 percent year-on-year in December (5.7 percent in the whole 1996 year), the Spanish market grew 14.7 percent (8.8 percent in 1996), Britain was up 8.5 percent (4.0 percent in 1996), and France 1.8 percent up (10.5 percent in 1996). Anfia noted France's car incentive scheme, which ended in November, was in operation in December 1995.
